english.title: Act as an unlicensed gangmaster
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) acted as a gangmaster in contravention of section 6 of the Gangmasters (Licensing) Act 2004
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12(1), (3) and (4) of the Gangmasters (Licensing) Act 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
acted as a gangmaster in contravention of s.6

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 12 provides "For this purpose a person acting as a gangmaster does not contravene section 6 by reason only of the fact that he breaches a condition of the licence which authorises him to so act".

other.penalty:
Either Way

Summary : maximum 6 / 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and /or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
Notes
(i) The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 12(3) of the Gangmasters (Licensing) Act 2004 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
(ii) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
